what: Add an "Open on phone" button to the "Start a workout on your phone" screen that opens MettleUp on the phone
why: The screen only tells the member to go and find the phone app; the watch already knows how to open a page on the phone (it does so for the Play Store), so one tap could take them straight there
impact_why: This is the first screen every member sees when they open the watch app outside a workout
my_view: My view: do it; it reuses the same open-on-phone call the "Get MettleUp on your phone" screen already makes, so it is small and low risk.

what: Turn "Workout saved" on the watch into a short summary: time taken, sets done, and any new personal best, for the same few seconds
why: Today the watch says only "Well done. See the details on your phone", so the reward moment happens on a phone that is in the bag; Hevy, Strong and Google's Fitbit app end a workout with a summary on the wrist (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Every finished workout of every watch user; a new-record line is a strong reason to come back
my_view: My view: worth doing after the watch app is public; the phone already works out these numbers at Finish, so it only needs to send three short lines with the saved signal.

what: Keep the heart rate the watch reads during a workout and save average and highest heart rate with the workout on the phone (and to Health Connect), after a clear yes from the member
why: The watch reads live heart rate only to show it and throws every reading away; members who wear a watch to the gym expect to see effort afterwards, which Hevy and Strong show from a watch (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Gives watch users a reason to keep wearing it and adds a number to their workout history
my_view: My view: good idea, but not before the privacy words are updated: heart rate is health data; keep it on the device, never send it to the gym, and ask once.

what: Add a Wear OS tile (swipe from the watch face) showing the last workout and "Open on phone to start"
why: The watch app has no tile and no watch-face corner at all, so a member who forgets it exists never sees MettleUp on the wrist until a workout pops it open; Google, Samsung and Fitbit fitness apps live in the tile carousel (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: A free daily reminder on the wrist, and a faster way back into the app than the app list
my_view: My view: do the tile (one read-only screen) once the watch app is public; skip a watch-face corner, the workout notice already puts an icon on the face during a workout.

what: When the phone does not answer, keep the set logged on the watch and send it as soon as the phone is back, instead of "Not saved, tick it on your phone"
why: A phone in a locker or out of range turns every watch tap into "Not saved", and the member has to redo the set on the phone later, which is the opposite of why they wear the watch
impact_why: Hits members who leave the phone in a locker, common in Indian gyms; today it teaches them the watch cannot be trusted
my_view: My view: worth it later, but only with care: the phone must refuse a set it already has, or the same set saves twice (an open finding already shows a set can be saved that was never done); do it after that is fixed.

what: Add "One more set" on the watch's "Exercise done" screen, next to Go
why: After the last planned set the only choice is Go to the next exercise; a member who wants an extra set has to pick up the phone, which breaks the hands-free flow
impact_why: Common in strength training, but not every workout
my_view: My view: maybe; ask a few watch users first whether they add sets often. The phone already supports adding a set, so the watch would send only one new action.

what: Let a member start a routine from the watch: show today's or the last routine with a Start button that opens the workout on the phone
why: The watch can only follow a workout the phone started; Hevy's and Strong's watch apps let a member start from the wrist (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Saves one phone unlock per workout; the member still needs the phone nearby for everything else
my_view: My view: not now; the cheap "Open on phone" button gets most of the value. Revisit when the watch app is public and has real users.

what: Show the weekly count on the watch after a workout, for example "3rd workout this week"
why: A streak line on the wrist is a small private nudge to come back, and the phone already counts workouts per week
impact_why: Small retention nudge, only for watch users
my_view: My view: fold it into the "Workout saved" summary idea rather than build it alone; one more line, no new screen.
